rule:
br-kp1in.40 lever: direct inbox read newest-first (written 2026-10-18, before any build or run of the lever).

Lever: sync::inbox::fetch_direct tries a newest-first walk of the project's message headers
(idx_messages_project_created pages, same paging as Jeff's shared reader b3c26ef0), probing the
agent's receipts per page (one (agent_id, message_id) index range read; 8-key batches when the range is
wide), and stops once the newest window is complete. It runs only when inbox_stats says the inbox spans
more than one receipt page (total_count >= 256), the window is small relative to it (limit*4 <= total),
and the recipient-side filter counts can fill the window (unread_count / ack_pending_count >= limit).
Its work (headers + receipts read) is capped at total_count/4; over the cap it falls back to the
existing full receipt scan. Both plans are exact; the counts only choose the plan. No schema change.
Constants (256, /4, *4) are fixed here from the cost model (one header + one receipt per row on
either plan), not tuned on any measurement.

Correctness gates (any failure = lever rejected):
- existing sync/inbox + project_mailbox tests unchanged and passing;
- new equality tests vs reference_inbox_rows_from_conn_impl: dense inbox, sparse inbox that exhausts
  the cap (fallback), IDs that do not follow created_ts (range too wide -> batches), equal-timestamp runs
  across pages, stale and missing inbox_stats, all filter combinations on the newest-first plan;
- db clippy --all-targets -D warnings; workspace prodcheck (lib+bins); conformance `it` full.

In-process measurement M (ignored test, release profile, same invocation, 5 alternating rounds, medians):
- M1 dense (agent receives 1 in 4 of the project's messages), own 10k, limit 20, unfiltered: new/old <= 0.50.
- M2 flatness: new(own 10k) <= 2 x new(own 1k), dense.
- G1 sparse guard (agent receives 1 in 100; own 1k; limit 20): new/old <= 1.35.
- G2 stale-hint guard (unread_count says >= limit but every unread row is older than the newest 2k
  headers; own 2k; unread_only): new/old <= 1.35.
M is a self-speedup (MAINTENANCE); it gates the code, it is not a campaign win.

Whole-server, vs incumbent, decisive for br-kp1in.40 (kp140_main_rule experiment unchanged):
mixed_rate.py, 2 senders A->B 4 sends/s, 2 closed-loop readers fetch_inbox(B, limit 20, mark_read=false),
1 search loop, 1 Hz health, 300 s, order A B B A, host lock. A = shipped v0.3.38 (build33/v038/am),
B = main + lever, portable release build, am SHA recorded per run. Validity: >= 1,140 of 1,200 sends.
  READS NOT SLOWER: pooled B read count >= 0.90 x A AND pooled B read p99 <= 1.5 x A -> br-kp1in.40 may
    close citing this run (with kp140_attr attribution).
  READS SLOWER otherwise -> bead stays open; lever still lands if M and the gates pass and the
    reported main-vs-lever late-window read p50 does not regress.
Reported, not deciding: Mode R (mark_read=true) A B B A; late-window (sends_before >= 600) read p50;
send p50/p99; the same probe on plain main (kp140_main result: 0.855x) for context.
Honesty note fixed now: the kp140 harness is the lever's best case (the reader receives every message);
G1/G2 are the guards for the cases it is not.

AMENDMENT (2026-10-18, still before any build or run): the newest-first plan is restricted to reads without a
read/ACK-state filter (unread_only, ack_required_only, ack_overdue). Reason found while writing tests, not from a
measurement: with those filters the receipt scan skips the header lookup of every filtered receipt, so it is cheap,
and the filtered rows can sit anywhere in history, so the walk's cost model does not hold. The hint is therefore
total_count only. G2 is replaced (the stale-unread case can no longer reach the walk):
- G2' header-filter guard: urgent_only on a dense inbox (1 in 4) where 1 in 50 of the agent's messages is urgent,
  own 2k, limit 20 (exhausts the cap -> fallback): new/old <= 1.35.
Everything else unchanged.
